analysis: The only changed lines in this file are 984-986 (head), in adaptersOnTheInstalledPath. The Gemma expected-environment dictionary now also includes DistributedInstalledPlan.batchLanesSwitch set to DistributedInstalledPlan.gemma4PipelineBatchLanes. The patch adds no production code, only a test expectation for a serial-prefill Gemma pipeline. I read the supplied units, which cover lines 1-664 of the file. The changed lines fall outside that range, so I did not see the adaptersOnTheInstalledPath body or how the dictionary is consumed. The surrounding test code (prefixSSDKeyNeverInChildEnvironment, metadataChecks) is unchanged context. It asserts security-relevant behavior for T-041 and the cache storage mitigations: the prefix-SSD key is passed only on the worker's stdin, never in arguments or environment, and the key file is owner-only. It also asserts that a stray decode switch is not forwarded, and that an unusable key file is left alone. The new batch-lanes environment variable is a non-secret integer tuning knob. It does not expose keys, prompts, or attestation material, and it widens no trust boundary visible here. Open question for the integration pass: the production nativeEnvironment/adapter code that sets batchLanesSwitch is not in this batch. Whether that env var can be overridden from ownerEnvironment, or affects the TB-007 resource bounds, has not been verified. This is not evidence of a regression.
